title: dynamic-batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce padding-induced wasted work in continuous batching by grouping requests by sequence-length buckets and tightening padding estimation. This improves throughput on mixed-length workloads and reduces per-token cost for common PLG use cases. This PR implements a sequence-length bucketing heuristic, integrates it with the continuous batching scheduler, adds conservative padding minimization and KV-cache-friendly bucket boundaries, and exposes a togglable config flag for canary rollouts. Changes are backwards-compatible by default and gated behind runtime config. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2145) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] microbenchmarks and canary run - [x] docs/console note and rollout plan Summary of changes and motivation: mixed-length traffic (short prompts and long completions) causes batching to pad to the longest sequence in a batch, substantially increasing GPU work for short requests. We implemented a lightweight bucketing strategy that groups requests into buckets by requested total sequence length (prompt + response cap). Buckets are selected using configurable boundaries derived from observed sequence-length percentiles (p50/p75/p95) and capped to avoid fragmentation. The scheduler now prefers same-bucket coalescing for batches within a small enqueue window, falling back to existing time/size thresholds for latency SLOs. To avoid KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal kernel selection, buckets align to kernel-friendly multiples and quantization-friendly sizes; we added a post-bucket normalization pass that nudges boundaries to the nearest supported kernel tile size. We also augment the scheduler with a conservative padding estimator that factors in recent prefix reuse to allow safe KV cache reuse when the prompt is identical or has known prefix prefixes. Implementation notes: - new module serving/runtime/batching/heuristics.py (Python): bucket heuristics, boundary calibration, tuning knobs - scheduler integration in serving/runtime/batching/scheduler.py: bucket-aware enqueue and eviction, metrics hooks - low-level kernel hinting in serving/runtime/kernel_selector/kernel_selector.cpp: map bucket size to preferred kernel and alignment - KV-cache reuse heuristics in serving/runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.go: mark cacheable prefixes and emit reusage metrics - tests in serving/runtime/batching/tests/test_bucketed_scheduler.py - perf harness updates in benchmark-lab/benchmarks/batching_seq_len.yaml Observability: added per-bucket metrics (requests, avg_padding_tokens, throughput, p50/p95 latency) and dashboards in observability-pack. We added an alert for unexpected bucket saturation and a dashboard panel showing padding savings. Performance results: microbenchmarks (A100, batchable mix workload) show ~28% increase in throughput and 18% reduction in average padding tokens for a 70/30 short/long traffic mix at 8k tokens/sec. End-to-end canary (10% traffic on dedicated pool for 48h) showed stable p50 latency and improved p95 by ~6%; no regressions in KV cache hit-rate observed. Rollout plan: start disabled, enable for internal tenants, canary across 10% of production traffic (Dedicated) for 48h, monitor per-bucket metrics and canary alerts, then gradual ramp to 100% with a 2h safety rollback window. Rollback procedure: set runtime flag to false; scheduler reverts to legacy batching path. Related work: follows up on prior PRs addressing dynamic batching heuristics and padding estimates. See also ENG-2431 for kernel alignment and tensorization work. Notes: this PR intentionally avoids aggressive bucket fragmentation and keeps a small number of buckets to maintain GPU utilization and scheduling simplicity.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can you explain the bucket boundary calibration and how it adapts to traffic shifts? I want to make sure we don't create tiny buckets that fragment GPU workloads.

Asha Patel: Boundaries are derived from a rolling histogram of observed total_seq_len percentiles (p50/p75/p95) with a floor/ceiling and a min bucket width. Calibration runs every 5 minutes by default and is rate-limited; we added safeguards so bucket changes only apply to new batches to avoid mid-batch churn.
Ruth Kim: Will kernel_selector changes affect existing kernel selection logic for pinned model revisions?

Asha Patel: Kernel hints are advisory and only used when a model variant exposes multiple kernels; we keep the legacy fallback path unchanged. We added unit tests to ensure identical kernels retain previous selection.
Samir Gupta: Observability looks good, but can we add a tag for requests that were forced into fallback (different bucket) to assist incident triage?
Asha Patel: Added a request tag and emitted an event metric request.bucket_fallback with reason strings (timeout/size/kv_mismatch).
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals. Added feature gate and rollout plan; no breaking changes. Perf wins observed in canary.
